area: Adversarial review of the agentskills#120 spec (the `_case_statuses` / `_guard` shell scanners in scripts/test_account_workflows.py, and the whitespace disagreement between account-skill-zips.yml's `case "$verdict" in` and account_zip_selection.py's normalise_status)

findings.claim: THE CANDIDATE `_case_statuses` REGRESSES A VALID-BASH REFORMAT THAT THE SHIPPED HELPER HANDLES. The spec's headline safety claim — "shapes the candidate gets WRONG: none" — is false. Wrap any `::warning::` string in the case block onto two lines (valid bash) and put a ` #` on the continuation — an issue reference such as `See #120`, which this repo's prose does constantly — and the candidate goes red while the shipped helper passes. Mechanism: `code()` strips comments with `_uncomment`, which is quote-aware PER LINE, so it cannot see that line 2 is inside a string and truncates it at the `#`, orphaning the opening `"`. `_mask_quoted` then tracks quotes across the WHOLE text, so from that orphaned quote onward everything is masked as data and the real `esac` is invisible. Composing a per-line stripper with a whole-text masker is the defect; the spec's residual-scope list mentions the per-line/whole-text difference and dismisses it as "correct for a `case` block". Worse, the message blames the case block for damage done ~15 lines upstream.
findings.evidence:
Same edit, same body, both helpers (real `_body()`, block replaced in memory, real assertion called):

  OLD (shipped, one line):  echo "::warning::the published account audit reads '$verdict' - the Tier-3 Routine has not published a usable result recently, ..." ;;
  NEW (wrapped, valid bash):
    echo "::warning::the published account audit reads: the Tier-3 Routine
    has not published a usable result recently. See #120 for the history." ;;

  [PRISTINE]  bash -n: VALID | code() kept line 2 as: 'has not published a usable result recently. See' | verdict: PASS
  [PATCHED]   bash -n: VALID | code() kept line 2 as: 'has not published a usable result recently. See' | verdict: AssertionError -> "the audit step's `case` has no closing `esac` outside a string and outside a nested `case`; this test cannot tell where the block ends, so its arms would be counted as absent"

(`code()`/`_uncomment` at scripts/test_account_workflows.py:46-109; the truncation is `_uncomment`'s documented per-line approximation, which was harmless while nothing downstream carried quote state across lines.)
findings.proposedChange:
Do not feed `_mask_quoted` the output of `code()`. Two options, and the spec must pick one explicitly:
(a) Mask FIRST on the raw body, then strip comments using the mask (a `#` is a comment only where the mask says it is code and the preceding char is start-of-line or whitespace). One walk, one quote model, no disagreement — and it strictly improves `code()` too.
(b) Keep `code()` but make `_mask_quoted` reset its quote state at each newline, matching `_uncomment` exactly. This loses multi-line strings but it is at least CONSISTENT, and it fails toward truncating rather than out-of-phase.
Either way, add this exact shape to `_ARMS_OK` as a required-PASS fixture — a wrapped `::warning::` whose continuation line contains ` #<number>` — because it is the one shape that distinguishes the two helper models and it is currently in neither the issue's six nor the spec's twenty-four.

findings.claim: FINDING 3's REACHABILITY STORY IS FALSE. The spec justifies the padded-verdict work with "A CRLF tail is the realistic delivery: skills-evals' artifact comes off a git checkout." It does not. `freshness_verdict` returns one of six Python STRING LITERALS; nothing from the checked-out `latest.json` reaches the returned status. The artifact's own `summary['status']` is interpolated only into the MESSAGE, which the workflow prints to stderr and never captures. So ` fresh` / `fresh\r` / `reported-failure\r` — every input in the spec's reproduction matrix except the empty capture — is unreachable through the path the spec names, and the spec never checks the producer.
findings.proposedChange: Rewrite FINDING 3's justification as defence-in-depth, not as a live bug: the shapes are unreachable TODAY because skills-evals returns literals, and the trim's value is that agentskills cannot see a change to that (AGENTS.md: "a rename INSIDE skills-evals moves a string no test here can see"). Keep the trim and the tests — the cost is two lines — but delete the CRLF-from-a-checkout claim from the PR body, and replace it with the reachability that IS real (next finding). Reviewers will check the producer, and a false reachability claim in the PR body is the part that loses the change its credibility.

findings.claim: THE ONE CONTAMINATION THAT IS REACHABLE IS THE ONE THE TRIM DOES NOT FIX — AND THE SPEC'S "THE INVARIANT" TEST PASSES ON IT. `verdict=$(python3 <<'PY' ... PY)` captures ALL stdout of the heredoc, so anything printing to stdout at import time inside skills-evals prepends a line. This is not hypothetical: account-skill-zips.yml:355-363 already carries a comment about exactly this fault for `drift`. With an extra line, `echo "status=$verdict"` writes a MULTI-LINE entry to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, whose second line has no `=` — the runner rejects the file command. The trim preserves interior whitespace by design, so it changes nothing, and the spec's third test reads only the first `status=` line and passes.

findings.proposedChange:
Add one assertion to test_the_step_and_the_module_agree_on_whitespace, before the two it already has, and add `'junk\nfresh'` and `sel.AUDIT_DRIFT_STATUS + '\njunk'` to its parametrize list:

    lines = [l for l in out.splitlines() if l]
    assert len(lines) == 1, (
        f"the step wrote {len(lines)} lines to $GITHUB_OUTPUT for "
        f"{verdict!r}: {out!r}. The runner parses that file line by line and "
        f"rejects a line with no `=`, so a stray stdout print inside the "
        f"heredoc takes the step out rather than degrading it."
    )

Then decide the shell fix deliberately: either keep only the LAST line of the capture (`verdict=${verdict##*$'\n'}`, matching what `print(status)` is supposed to be the last of), or reject a multi-line capture into the empty-capture branch, which already has the right diagnosis text ("what broke is the import inside this step"). Say which, and why, in the PR body — this is the fault the step is actually exposed to.

findings.claim: openQuestion 3 STATES A FALSEHOOD IN THE SAFE DIRECTION: "Both annotate, so no run goes from loud to quiet." A run does. With `results_ok=no`, ` not-yet-bootstrapped` annotates today (it falls to `*)`) and annotates NOTHING after the trim (it reaches its own arm, whose `echo` sits inside `if [ "$results_ok" = yes ]`). Loud to silent is the exact failure class this whole step exists to prevent. And the spec's own proposed test cannot see it: `test_whitespace_around_a_verdict_changes_nothing` calls `self._run` twice with the default `results_ok="yes"` on both sides.
findings.evidence:
Real `_run` harness, both trees, `_run(tmp, verdict, results_ok=...)`:

[PRISTINE]  verdict=' not-yet-bootstrapped'  results_ok=no   warns=1
[WITH-TRIM] verdict=' not-yet-bootstrapped'  results_ok=no   warns=0   <-- loud -> quiet
[PRISTINE]  verdict='not-yet-bootstrapped\r' results_ok=no   warns=1
[WITH-TRIM] verdict='not-yet-bootstrapped\r' results_ok=no   warns=0   <-- loud -> quiet

(results_ok=yes is 1 -> 1 on every row, which is all the spec measured.)
The conditional is .github/workflows/account-skill-zips.yml:434-436:
              if [ "$results_ok" = yes ]; then
                echo "::warning::the published account audit reads '$verdict', but the eval-results branch cloned cleanly - ..."
              fi ;;
findings.proposedChange:
(1) Correct the open question: the trim moves ` not-yet-bootstrapped` from a run that annotates to one that does not whenever `results_ok=no`. State the mitigation honestly rather than the false absolute — the clone failure IS annotated in the step head, which `_tail()` excludes, so production is not silent; the harness is. That distinction belongs in the PR body because it is the reason the change is acceptable.
(2) Make the test able to see it. Parametrize the existing test over the flag instead of taking its default:

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("results_ok", ["yes", "no"])
    ...
    bare_log, bare_out = self._run(bare, verdict, results_ok=results_ok)
    pad_log, pad_out = self._run(padded, pad.format(verdict), results_ok=results_ok)

Run it before the trim and confirm the `results_ok="no"` rows are the ones that newly red; that is the proof the assertion is load-bearing.

findings.claim: THE PROPOSED `_guard` NEGATIVE CONTROL DETECTS A STRICT SUBSET OF A TEST THAT ALREADY EXISTS. `test_the_refusal_tests_are_not_passing_on_broken_bash` asserts only `bash -n` exit 0. Every state it fires on is a state where the snippet refuses a real name, which reds all four `test_it_admits_every_real_declared_name` cases first — the spec's own evidence table says so (`admits=RED` on all four vacuous shapes). Meanwhile the vacuity mode it is described as guarding — "a suite that asserts nothing about the injection guard" — is reachable through valid bash, where the control passes.
findings.evidence:
$ # a guard that is valid bash and refuses EVERYTHING
$ broken='case "$SKILL" in *) exit 1 ;; esac'
spec control (bash -n) on a refuse-everything guard: PASSES
  SKILL='sync-skills'    rc=1  (refused)
  SKILL='sync-skills;id' rc=1  (refused)
  SKILL=''               rc=1  (refused)

$ # the truncated slice the control targets
$ trunc='case "$SKILL" in *) exit 1 ;;'
spec control on a TRUNCATED slice: FIRES
  and test_it_admits_every_real_declared_name already sees rc = 2 (red)

So: control fires => admits already red. Control silent =/=> guard sound.
findings.proposedChange:
Drop the `bash -n` control and assert the property that actually distinguishes a working slice from a vacuous one — that the extracted snippet is the SKILL guard and reads its input:

    def test_the_extracted_guard_is_the_one_that_reads_SKILL(self):
        snippet = self._guard()
        assert snippet.count('case "$SKILL"') == 1 and snippet.rstrip().endswith("esac"), snippet
        # and the discriminating pair, in one place, so trimming the admit
        # list below cannot leave the refusals proving nothing:
        assert self._run(snippet, "sync-skills") == 0, snippet
        assert self._run(snippet, "sync-skills;id") != 0, snippet

That catches both the truncated slice AND the refuse-everything slice, which `bash -n` cannot.

findings.claim: THE `_guard` PROPOSAL'S OPENER LOOKUP RAISES `StopIteration`, NOT AN AssertionError, AND ITS NEW TEST DOES NOT COMPILE AS WRITTEN. The spec gives `_case_statuses` a `next(..., None)` plus a diagnostic assert and then writes `_guard`'s twin as a bare `next(...)` — a naked StopIteration with no message, in a file whose every other assert carries a sentence explaining what broke. Separately, the verbatim negative-control test body uses `tmp_path` but the signature is `(self)`; the spec relegates the fix to a parenthetical after the code block.

findings.proposedChange: Use the `next(..., None)` + assert form in `_guard` too, with a message naming the same failure the `_case_statuses` twin names ("the skill guard's `case \"$SKILL\"` is no longer a command this test can find; the snippet below would be empty, and an empty snippet exits 0 and ADMITS everything"). Note that an empty slice is the opposite failure from a truncated one and is the silent-green direction — worth its own sentence. And put `tmp_path` in the signature of any test that uses it rather than in prose beside it; a spec that says "Verbatim" has to be pasteable.

findings.claim: THE SPEC FIXES TWO SHELL SCANNERS AND LEAVES A THIRD THAT ALL OF FINDING 3 RESTS ON. `_tail()` locates the whole verdict-handling region with a plain `body.index(') || verdict=""')` — the same unanchored substring search the spec is removing from `_case_statuses` and `_guard`, in the same class, in the same file. Every FINDING 3 test executes whatever that returns, and FINDING 3's own fix makes it MORE load-bearing by inserting the two trim lines immediately after that marker. A fourth, `body.index(line)` at :375, takes the first occurrence of a line's text and would check the wrong `gh api` call if two were identical. The spec's framing ("the two scanners") and openQuestion 1 ("Two call sites is the threshold") are both counting wrong.

findings.proposedChange: Answer openQuestion 1 with "yes, factor it" — but factor it for FOUR call sites, not two, and say so. `_tail` at :608 gets the same treatment as the other two: find the marker in `code(body)` confirmed against the mask, so a comment quoting `) || verdict=""` cannot relocate the slice. Add a regression case for it in the same change — splice a comment `# the heredoc ends with ) || verdict=""` ABOVE the real marker and assert `_tail()` still returns the real tail — because FINDING 3's entire test suite is downstream of that one index() call, and a mis-slice there makes all 53 of the new tests pass against a region that is not the step.

findings.claim: COVERAGE MISS THE SPEC WALKED PAST: `case "$FROM_RUN"` at record-account-upload.yml:59 has NO test at all. findings.claim: THE REGRESSION SET IS SPECIFIED WITH THREE DIFFERENT SIZES AND THE WRONG NUMBER OF NEGATIVE CONTROLS, SO NOBODY CAN TELL WHEN IT IS DONE. The spec calls it "Sixteen parametrize cases plus two negative controls", then "All 18 measured", then numbers 18 entries in which #16 is itself four shapes (so 21), then openQuestion 5 calls them "The eight `_ARMS_OK` fixtures". The must-stay-red block lists three cases while the claim says two. For a change whose entire value is a locked-down fixture list, the fixture list is the one thing that has to be countable.

FINDING 2(e) proposedChange: entries numbered 1..18, with "16  $(...) in a body / blank lines / no trailing ;; / CRLF (four more, cheap)"
FINDING 2(e) must-stay-red block: three parametrize entries ("a rogue arm", "the drift arm through an UNQUOTED expansion", "no catch-all arm at all")
openQuestions[4]: "The eight `_ARMS_OK` fixtures need a home."
findings.proposedChange:
State one number and make the test enforce it. Split #16 into its four entries, add the wrapped-string-with-`#` shape from finding 1, and lock the count so a future edit cannot quietly delete a fixture:

    def test_the_regression_set_did_not_shrink(self):
        assert len(self._ARMS_OK) == 22, (
            "a shape was removed from the set that proves this helper reads "
            "bash rather than text; removing one is how the six false reds "
            "got here"
        )

And answer openQuestion 5 as specified (in-memory `_splice`, no fixture files) — that part is right: `plugins/*/skills/*/tests/` is a CI glob and a `tests/fixtures/` dir under scripts/ would need its own salient-path entry in ci.yml.

findings.proposedChange: Cut the environment paragraph from the PR body or scope it to the container it was measured in ("in the session I ran this in, ..."). It is not a repo defect and it is not universal, and stating it as a property of "a fresh remote worktree" sends the next reader to install packages they already have. Keep the 962/exit-0 baseline — it reproduces exactly, and it is the number every other measurement in the spec hangs off.

findings.claim: WHAT IS SOUND, verified rather than taken on trust, so the fix is not re-litigated: the reproduction is accurate and the two corrections the spec makes to the issue are both real. R IS position-dependent, nested `case` IS a false red before the catch-all and a pass in the last arm, and the candidate closes eleven shapes without breaking the negative controls or the 962 baseline. The `_guard` refactor is byte-for-byte behaviour-preserving on today's workflow.

findings.proposedChange: No change. Recorded so the sound half of the spec is not re-derived: keep the nesting-counted walk (an anchored closer alone does regress nested-late, as the spec says), keep `_unquote` in the `else` branch only, keep the `an unquoted $drift still FAILs` control, and keep the two-line shell trim over dropping normalise_status' strip. The findings above are corrections to that design, not a case against it.

openQuestions: Which quote model wins — mask-first-then-strip-comments, or a per-line `_mask_quoted`? Finding 1 says the current pairing cannot stand, but the choice is a real trade: mask-first is one walk and strictly better, and it also changes `code()`, which is the helper eleven other assertions in the file rest on (`TestTheCommentStripperTheseAssertionsRestOn` exists precisely because it is load-bearing). That makes it a wider blast radius than the spec scoped for. Per-line masking is the contained option and gives up multi-line strings. Decide before implementation, because the `_ARMS_OK` fixture list differs between them.

Does the FINDING 3 shell fix want to handle a multi-line capture, or only surrounding whitespace? The trim as specified leaves the one reachable contamination (an extra stdout line from inside the heredoc) writing a $GITHUB_OUTPUT the runner rejects. Handling it means choosing a policy — last line wins, or route it to the empty-capture branch — and that is a behaviour decision about what a corrupted capture MEANS, not a formatting one.

Is `results_ok=no` + a padded `not-yet-bootstrapped` worth blocking on? The trim makes that combination silent in the harness. Production still annotates the clone failure in the step head, so the run is not truly quiet — but `_tail()` cannot see the head, so no test in this file can distinguish the two. Either the harness grows a whole-step runner for the verdict path, or the PR body states the limitation plainly. It should not be left as the false absolute the spec currently asserts.

Should the FROM_RUN guard's missing coverage ride in this PR or its own? It is genuinely a separate defect from the two the issue names, but it is five lines once `_shell_block` exists, and splitting it means the shared helper lands with two call sites and the third arrives later — which is the drift the spec's own openQuestion 1 is worried about.

One PR or two (the spec's own question): the evidence now says TWO, and not for the reason the spec gives. FINDING 2's fix has a live regression to resolve (finding 1) and touches the file's central quote model; FINDING 3's fix is two shell lines with an independent verifier and a reachability story that needs rewriting but not re-engineering. Coupling them makes the cheap, correct half wait on the expensive, contested half.
